arxiv-2106-09893.title: Propagation-induced limits to high harmonic generation in 3D Dirac semimetals
arxiv-2106-09893.creator: Jeremy Lim, Yee Sin Ang, Lay Kee Ang, Liang Jie Wong
arxiv-2106-09893.description: Abstract 3D Dirac semimetals (DSMs) are promising materials for terahertz high harmonic generation (HHG). We show that 3D DSMs’ high nonlinearity opens up a regime of nonlinear optics where extreme subwavelength current density features develop within nanoscale propagation distances of the driving field.

arxiv-2306-13683.title: Model Families for Multi-Criteria Decision Support: A COVID-19 Case Study
arxiv-2306-13683.creator: Martin Bicher, Claire Rippinger, Christoph Urach, Dominik Brunmeir, Melanie Zechmeister, Niki Popper
arxiv-2306-13683.description: Abstract Continued model-based decision support is associated with particular challenges, especially in long-term projects. Due to the regularly changing questions and the often changing understanding of the underlying system, the models used must be regularly re-evaluated, -modelled and -implemented with respect to changing modelling purpose, system boundaries and mapped causalities.

arxiv-2310-05300.title: Which model density is best in pair natural orbital local correlation theory?
arxiv-2310-05300.creator: Réka A. Horváth, Kesha Sorathia, Isabelle Saint, David P. Tew
arxiv-2310-05300.description: Abstract Low-scaling electron correlation theory based on the pair natural orbital approximation, PNO-CCSD(T), has become a powerful computational tool. Motivated by the recent discovery of large errors for organometallic molecules, we assess the role of the model density used to discard unimportant contributions.

arxiv-2410-00843.title: Ab initio computations of atomic nuclei
arxiv-2410-00843.creator: T. Papenbrock
arxiv-2410-00843.description: Abstract Ab initio computations of atomic nuclei, based on Hamiltonians from effective field theories of quantum chromodynamics, are now routinely used to predict and describe properties of medium heavy nuclei, and even the heavy nucleus 208 Pb has been reached.

arxiv-2508-16671.title: RePro: Reflective Paper-to-Code Reproduction Enabled by Fine-Grained Verification
arxiv-2508-16671.creator: Mingyang Zhou, Quanming Yao, Lun Du, Lanning Wei, Da Zheng
arxiv-2508-16671.description: Abstract Reproducing machine learning papers is essential for scientific progress but remains challenging for both humans and automated agents. Existing agent-based methods often struggle to fully and accurately reproduce implementation details such as mathematical formulas and algorithmic logic. Previous studies show that reflection with explicit feedback improves agent performance. However, current paper reproduction methods fail to effectively adopt this strategy.

arxiv-2509-00718.title: Exam Readiness Index (ERI): A Theoretical Framework for a Composite, Explainable Index
arxiv-2509-00718.creator: Ananda Prakash Verma
arxiv-2509-00718.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ananda Prakash Verma. We present a theoretical framework for an Exam Readiness Index (ERI): a composite, blueprint-aware score R ∈ [ 0,100 ] R\in[0,100] that summarizes a learner’s readiness for a high-stakes exam while remaining interpretable and actionable.

arxiv-2510-10340.title: Picoflares in the Quiet Solar Corona
arxiv-2510-10340.creator: O. Podladchikova ,, A. Warmuth, L. Harra, L. Dolla, C. Verbeeck, M. Mierla, L. Rodriguez, S. Parenti, F. Auchère, M. K. Georgoulis, S. J. Hofmeister, N. Engler, M. J. West, R. Aznar Cuadrado, A. M. Veronig, P. Antolin, S. Purkhart, D. M. Long, É. Buchlin, M. Haberreiter, K. Velli, A. N. Zhukov, H. S
arxiv-2510-10340.description: Abstract Context. X-ray observations of the Sun prompted Eugene Parker to introduce the concept of ”nanoflares” as fundamental energy release units in the solar corona, with estimated energies of 10 24 10^{24} erg from current dissipation in 10,000 km loops. Parker anticipated that even smaller flares would be detectable with improved instrumentation.

pmc-11372478.title: Supportive care needs, quality of life and social support among elderly colorectal cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy: a longitudinal study
pmc-11372478.creator: Siqin Lian, Xijie Hou, Weichen Liu, Ming Li, Guolian Chen, Ying Ling
pmc-11372478.description: ObjectiveThe purpose of this study is to examine the changes in supportive care needs, quality of life and social support during different chemotherapy cycles among elderly colorectal cancer patients.MethodsThis prospective longitudinal study recruited 160 elderly colorectal cancer patients using convenience sampling at a hospital in Guangxi between August 2023 and April 2024.

pmc-11433836.title: A Bis(Acridino)-Crown Ether for Recognizing Oligoamines in Spermine Biosynthesis
pmc-11433836.creator: Péter Kisfaludi, Sára Spátay, Marcell Krekó, Panna Vezse, Tünde Tóth, Péter Huszthy, Ádám Golcs, Alexander F Khlebnikov
pmc-11433836.description: Oligoamines in cellular metabolism carry extremely diverse biological functions (i.e., regulating Ca2+-influx, neuronal nitric oxide synthase, membrane potential, Na+, K+-ATPase activity in synaptosomes, etc.). Furthermore, they also act as longevity agents and have a determinative role in autophagy, cell growth, proliferation, and death, while oligoamines dysregulation is a key in a variety of cancers.

pmc-11443677.title: Efficacy of an internet-based guided trauma-focused intervention in reducing ICD-11 posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms: study protocol of a randomized controlled trial
pmc-11443677.creator: Odeta Gelezelyte, Greta Guogaite, Auguste Nomeikaite, Jonathan I. Bisson, Catrin Lewis, Evaldas Kazlauskas
pmc-11443677.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPosttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a common mental disorder. However, many cases of PTSD remain untreated because of limited healthcare resources and other treatment-seeking barriers. Effective internet-based interventions could help to improve access to PTSD treatments. Therefore, the main objective of the planned randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the efficacy of the Lithuanian version of the guided internet-based self-help programme (Spring) in reducing ICD-11 PTSD symptoms.MethodsThe planned sample size is 50 participants exposed to different traumatic experiences.

pmc-11492998.title: Construction and validation of a comprehensive metabolism-associated prognostic model for predicting survival and immunotherapy benefits in ovarian cancer
pmc-11492998.creator: Wei Ye, Yuanyuan Fang, Zhaolian Wei
pmc-11492998.description: Background: Ovarian cancer (OV) is a prevalent malignancy among gynecological tumors. Numerous metabolic pathways play a significant role in various human diseases, including malignant tumors. Our study aimed to develop a prognostic signature for OV based on a comprehensive set of metabolism-related genes (MRGs).Method: To achieve this, a bioinformatics analysis was performed on the expression profiles of 51 MRGs.

pmc-11495876.title: ATP-induced reconfiguration of the micro-viscoelasticity of cardiac and skeletal myosin solutions
pmc-11495876.creator: Pablo Domínguez-García, Jose R Pinto, Ana Akrap, Sylvia Jeney
pmc-11495876.description: We study the high-frequency, micro-mechanical response of suspensions composed of cardiac and skeletal muscle myosin by optical trapping interferometry. We observe that in low ionic strength solutions, upon the addition of magnesium adenosine triphosphate (MgATP2−), myosin suspensions radically change their micro-mechanics properties, generating a viscoelastic fluid characterized by a complex modulus similar to a suspension of worm-like micelles.

pmc-11574162.title: EphrinB2-mediated CDK5/ISL1 pathway enhances cardiac lymphangiogenesis and alleviates ischemic injury by resolving post-MI inflammation
pmc-11574162.creator: Yingnan Bai, Liming Chen, Fanghao Guo, Jinghong Zhang, Jinlin Hu, Xuefei Tao, Qing Lu, Wenyi Li, Xueying Chen, Ting Gong, Nan Qiu, Yawei Jin, Lifan Yang, Yu Lei, Chengchao Ruan, Qing Jing, John P. Cooke, Shijun Wang, Yunzeng Zou, Junbo Ge
pmc-11574162.description: EphrinB2 (erythropoietin-producing hepatoma interactor B2) is a key Eph/ephrin family member, promoting angiogenesis, vasculogenesis, and lymphangiogenesis during embryonic development. However, the role of EphrinB2 in cardiac lymphangiogenesis following myocardial infarction (MI) and the potential molecular mechanism remains to be demonstrated. This study revealed that EphrinB2 prevented ischemic heart post-MI from remodeling and dysfunction by activating the cardiac lymphangiogenesis signaling pathway.

pmc-11577497.title: Effect of Anchorage Modifications on the Efficacy of Miniscrew-Assisted Rapid Palatal Expansion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11577497.creator: Yury A Villa-Obando, Sandra M Correa-Osorio, Robinson A Castrillon-Marin, Anny M Vivares-Builes, Carlos M Ardila
pmc-11577497.description: Mini-implant-assisted rapid palatal expansion (MARPE) offers a non-surgical alternative for expanding the basal bone, increasing skeletal effects while minimizing undesirable dental side effects. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the effectiveness of MARPE in terms of transverse skeletal development, dentoalveolar changes, and periodontal effects, with consideration of appliance design.

pmc-11603859.title: Dosimetric effects of prone immobilization devices on skin in intensity-modulated radiation therapy for gynecologic cancer: a retrospective study
pmc-11603859.creator: Donghui Wang, Bin Li, Luxi Chen, Zhenghuan Li, Fantu Kong, Huamei Yan, Xiangying Xu, Jie Dong
pmc-11603859.description: ObjectiveThe dose perturbation effect of immobilization devices is often overlooked in intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) for gynecologic cancer. This retrospective study assessed the dosimetric effects of a prone immobilization device combined with a belly board (PIDBB) on the skin.MethodsWe recruited 63 women with gynecologic cancer undergoing postoperative IMRT at our institute. A 0.

pmc-11672419.title: Multiple Typing Approach to Characterize Toxoplasma gondii Strains from Captive and Livestock Species in Northern Italy Suggests the Circulation of Type-II Variants
pmc-11672419.creator: Filippo Maria Dini, Martha Ynés Salas-Fajardo, Roberta Taddei, Mattia Ramini, Silvia Vianello, Monica Caffara, Roberta Galuppi
pmc-11672419.description: Simple SummaryToxoplasma gondii is a common parasite that spreads through food and affects both humans and animals worldwide. Understanding the genetic makeup of this parasite is important because it helps us learn more about its spread and effects on health. This study looked at samples from northern Italy to better understand the genetics of T.

pmc-12719175.title: Characterization of volatiles in tea leaf cuticular wax during white tea processing across distinct climatic regions
pmc-12719175.creator: Dandan Qi, Min Lu, Xingmin Zhang, Lin Yue, Yali Shi, Houzhen Jia, Chunwang Dong, Changbo Yuan
pmc-12719175.description: Climate change significantly impacts tea plant (Camellia sinensis) physiology, particularly the cuticular wax layer on leaves, which serves as a critical barrier against environmental stress. This study investigates how climatically distinct growing regions modify the composition and morphology of tea leaf cuticular wax, and thereby affect volatile organic compounds (VOCs) during white tea processing.

pmc-12999425.title: Senescence-related epicardial adipocyte genes lead to immune infiltration and myocardial infarction progression
pmc-12999425.creator: Zhihuan Dong, Limin Wang, Yuheng Lang, Ruiying Zhang, Yuchao Wang, Chengxiu Zhao, Qingliang Chen, Yue Zheng
pmc-12999425.description: BackgroundAfter coronary artery disease (CAD)-related myocardial injury, reactivation of the epicardium results in cardiac remodeling via paracrine secretion. However, the senescence-related genomic signature that reflects epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) and immune infiltration is not well understood.MethodsAdipocyte-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified in EAT and subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) from patients with and without CAD.

pmc-13233784.title: Concurrent Von Hippel-Lindau disease and enhanced S-cone syndrome leading to a distinct retinal phenotype
pmc-13233784.creator: Maram AlEnazi, Abdulrahman H. Badawi, Wael A. Alsakran, Moustafa S. Magliyah
pmc-13233784.description: BackgroundVon Hippel–Lindau (VHL) disease and Enhanced S-cone syndrome (ESCS) are rare inherited disorders that independently predispose to vision-threatening retinal pathology through distinct mechanisms: VHL through hypoxia-induced activation of several angiogenic factors, which lead to the development of retinal capillary hemangioblastoma (RCH), and ESCS by disrupting photoreceptor development through NR2E3 variants.

pmc-13384828.title: Holding on to tradition: continuation of ethnic and festival food traditions by Nepalese students in the United States
pmc-13384828.creator: Anu Karki, Shuyang Qu, Fally Masambuka-Kanchewa, Daniela Dimitrova
pmc-13384828.description: IntroductionTraditional foodways can help international students preserve cultural continuity and cope emotionally and socially in a new environment, while limited access to traditional foods leads to cultural disconnection and a negative impact on mental wellbeing. This study explored what ethnic and festival foods and practices Nepalese international students retain in the U.S.

pmc-13518966.title: Motivational interviewing chatbot improves lifestyle in primary healthcare settings in a pragmatic randomised controlled trial
pmc-13518966.creator: Clive Ho Yin Wong, Mabel Ngai Kiu Wong, Wai Kai Hou, Fridolin Sze Thou Ting, Yuk Mun Ng, Chetwyn Che Hin Chan
pmc-13518966.description: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) impose escalating demands on community-based primary healthcare (PHC) systems globally. Motivational interviewing (MI) is effective but difficult to scale due to resource and training constraints. We conducted the first pragmatic trial evaluating whether an automated chatbot operationalising MI principles could improve lifestyle behaviours when integrated into routine PHC settings.

pmc-13668968.title: Late transfer to seawater improves intestinal development of osmoregulatory capacity in Atlantic salmon smolts
pmc-13668968.creator: Raneesha de Fonseka, Marius Takvam, Kristina Sundell, Elisabeth Jönsson, Tom Ole Nilsen, Vibeke Vikeså, Henrik Sundh
pmc-13668968.description: The development and function of intestinal fluid transport capacity in Atlantic salmon, determine seawater (SW) readiness, but poorly understood in modern aquaculture practices. This study aimed to investigate the development of intestinal fluid transport capacity during smoltification and the effect of short-term fasting and a high-lipid diet.
